subject: ophthalmology
title: Strabismus, amblyopia and nystagmus

steps.tx: **Comitant squint** keeps the deviation equal in all gazes. **Infantile esotropia** appears before six months as a large angle inward turn with cross fixation, dissociated vertical deviation and latent nystagmus, and it needs early surgery with glasses. **Accommodative esotropia** affects hypermetropic toddlers who over converge, so full hypermetropic glasses straighten refractive cases while partly accommodative cases keep a residual angle for surgery. **Intermittent exotropia** drifts outward with bright sunlight closure and better near control, and deteriorating control earns surgery. Cover and prism testing with Hirschberg estimation measures the angle.
steps.say: When the inward turn measures the same in every gaze direction, the squint is comitant and the lesson points to infantile esotropia in a young infant. That baby shows a large angle turn before six months with cross fixation, and associated dissociated vertical deviation with latent nystagmus pushes toward early surgery. A hypermetropic toddler who turns inward while fixing at near usually has accommodative esotropia, so full plus glasses come first. An older child who drifts outward in bright sunlight but controls the eyes at near has intermittent exotropia, which is watched until control slips.

steps.tx: The photograph shows an infant with a **large angle esotropia** of the left eye that turns frankly inward while the right eye fixes. The deviation stays equal across gazes, which marks it as a **comitant squint**, and the upward drift of the nonfixing eye reflects **dissociated vertical deviation**. This combination of early onset inward turn with dissociated vertical deviation defines infantile esotropia, so the child needs cycloplegic refraction with glasses first and then early strabismus surgery to align the eyes.
steps.say: Look at this infant and notice the left eye turned frankly inward while the right eye fixes on the camera. The deviation is comitant because the angle stays the same in every gaze direction. The fellow eye also drifts upward, which is the dissociated vertical deviation that accompanies infantile esotropia. For the exam, link a large angle inward turn before six months with cross fixation and dissociated vertical deviation, and remember that glasses come first and early surgery follows.

steps.tx: **Paralytic squint** changes with gaze and looks worst when the patient looks toward the weak muscle, producing diplopia with a compensatory head posture. **Sixth nerve palsy** blocks abduction so esotropia grows with face turn toward the palsy. **Fourth nerve palsy** causes hypertropia that worsens on downgaze and head tilt to the opposite side, and the Parks Bielschowsky three step test isolates superior oblique weakness. Third nerve palsy adds exotropia with hypotropia, ptosis and a dilated pupil. Thyroid eye disease and myasthenia mimic palsies through lid signs and fatigability.
steps.say: When double vision worsens in one direction of gaze, the squint is paralytic and the patient turns the head to escape the diplopia. A sixth nerve palsy stops the eye from abducting, so the inward turn grows on lateral gaze. A fourth nerve palsy lifts one eye higher, and the hypertropia worsens on downgaze and on tilt toward the opposite side. The three step test then isolates the weak superior oblique muscle. Thyroid disease and myasthenia can mimic a palsy, so lid signs and fatigability must be checked.

steps.tx: **Amblyopia** dulls vision in one eye during the childhood critical period up to about seven or eight years, when strabismus, anisometropia or visual deprivation disrupts development. Deprivation from cataract or ptosis needs urgent clearance, while refractive causes start with glasses. **Occlusion patching** of the good eye for hours set by age and depth then forces use of the lazy eye, and atropine penalisation of the good eye offers an alternative with close review for reverse amblyopia. Photoscreeners and the red reflex catch cases before school, since adult discovery rarely recovers.
steps.say: A lazy eye that never learned to see in childhood is amblyopia, and the critical period closes around seven or eight years. Strabismus, unequal refractive error and deprivation from cataract or ptosis are the triggers, so glasses come first for refractive causes. The good eye is then patched for set hours or blurred with atropine, which forces the lazy eye to work. Deprivation needs urgent surgery before patching, and screening with photoscreeners and the red reflex catches children in time.

steps.tx: **Nystagmus** oscillates the eyes from birth or from acquired disease. Infantile idiopathic nystagmus stays conjugate and horizontal with a null point and head turn but no oscillopsia, while latent nystagmus beats nasally in the uncovered eye. **Spasmus nutans** brings the infantile triad of nystagmus with head nodding and torticollis yet stays benign with selected imaging. Vestibular nystagmus jerks away from the lesion with vertigo and nausea, gaze evoked forms follow drugs or cerebellar disease, and downbeat nystagmus points to the craniocervical junction while upbeat forms implicate the cerebellar vermis.
steps.say: Dancing eyes present from birth without dizziness usually mean infantile nystagmus, which is conjugate and horizontal with a null point. New dancing with vertigo and nausea points to the vestibular system and needs brain imaging. Drug induced and cerebellar forms appear on eccentric gaze, and see saw or pendular patterns in multiple sclerosis deserve the same workup. Downbeat nystagmus implicates the craniocervical junction, while upbeat nystagmus implicates the cerebellar vermis.
